claims.text: Molecular dynamics simulations can be used to study the size-dependent thermal response of FeCuCrCoNi high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles.
The effective thermal-transition temperature of FeCuCrCoNi nanoparticles increases with particle size.
The temperature for the onset of significant atomic diffusion in FeCuCrCoNi nanoparticles increases with particle size.
Increasing nanoparticle size reduces the surface-to-volume ratio.
The proposed initial nanoparticles are compositionally uniform FeCuCrCoNi high-entropy alloys.
Thermal response can be compared across particle sizes by gradually increasing temperature in MD simulations.
The simulations should use a controlled heating rate and an interatomic potential appropriate for the alloy.
The fraction of undercoordinated atoms changes with nanoparticle surface-to-volume ratio.
The fraction of undercoordinated atoms mediates nanoparticle thermal stability.
Smaller nanoparticles have a higher proportion of surface atoms with lower coordination.
A higher proportion of low-coordination surface atoms promotes atomic diffusion and structural reorganization at lower temperatures.
Larger nanoparticles contain more bulk-like regions than smaller nanoparticles.
Larger nanoparticles require higher temperatures to attain atomic mobility and structural transformation comparable to those of smaller nanoparticles.
Larger FeCuCrCoNi nanoparticles will exhibit higher melting or significant-diffusion temperatures.
A standard-size or bulk-like benchmark has greater thermal stability than very small nanoparticles.
The predicted trend is limited to the studied size range and simulation conditions.
The magnitude of the transition-temperature shift is sensitive to the interatomic potential and simulation parameters.
